entries.meaning: To choose someone for a public office by voting. ---
examples: Americans elect a president every four years.
She was elected to the state senate in 2022.
The district has never elected a Democrat.
entries.contrast: You are elected to an office and elected as something: elected to the council, elected as chairman.

entries.meaning: To officially name someone as a candidate for an office or an honor. ---
examples: Each party will nominate a candidate in the summer.
The president nominated her for a federal judgeship.
He has been nominated three times and lost twice.
entries.contrast: You nominate someone for a post or as a candidate.

entries.meaning: To ask a sample of people what they think, or to score a certain result in such a survey. ---
examples: Networks poll voters right outside the precinct.
The paper polled a thousand adults last week.
He is polling well in the suburbs.
entries.русский: опрашивать, проводить опрос; набирать (голоса в опросах)
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (poll likely voters), intransitive (she is polling at 40 percent)
entries.contrast: The verb poll sounds exactly like pole.

entries.meaning: To officially control and run a country, a state, or a city. ---
examples: It is easier to campaign than to govern.
The party governed for twelve years.
The island has been governed from the mainland since 1898.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (govern a country), intransitive (it is harder to govern)
entries.contrast: The o sounds like the u in cup: GUV-urn, not GOH-vurn.

entries.meaning: To put someone into office with a formal public ceremony. ---
examples: The state will inaugurate its new governor in January.
He was inaugurated on a cold, rainy Monday.
The country has inaugurated four presidents in six years.

entries.meaning: To rule as a king or a queen. ---
examples: Few monarchs reign for more than fifty years.
She reigned for seven decades.
He had reigned only a year when the war began.
entries.contrast: reign (rule) sounds exactly like rain and rein, and it is spelled with -eign.

entries.meaning: To give a person or a body the legal power to do something. ---
examples: The law empowers the governor to call out the guard.
Congress empowered the agency to write the rules.
Local boards have been empowered to set their own budgets.

entries.meaning: To call a formal meeting, or to come together for one. ---
examples: The legislature will convene in January.
The governor convened a special session.
The panel has convened twice this month.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (convene a session), intransitive (the committee convenes Monday)

entries.meaning: To lead a committee or a meeting as its head. ---
examples: She will chair the committee next session.
He chaired the hearing for six straight hours.
The panel is chaired by a retired judge.
entries.contrast: Same word as the piece of furniture; as a verb it means to run a meeting.

entries.meaning: To have the power to decide what an institution or a place does. ---
examples: One party will control both chambers next year.
Rebels controlled the capital for a week.
Prices here are controlled by the state.
entries.contrast: The l doubles before an ending, in American English too: control → controlled → controlling.

entries.meaning: To make laws. ---
examples: Congress cannot legislate good manners.
The state legislated a higher minimum wage.
Term limits were legislated in the 1990s.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (legislate a higher wage), intransitive (Congress cannot legislate on it)

entries.meaning: To delay or stop a vote in the US Senate by talking at great length. ---
examples: A senator can filibuster almost any bill.
They filibustered for eleven hours straight.
The nomination is being filibustered by two members.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (filibuster the bill), intransitive (they filibustered all night)

entries.meaning: To put a law, a plan, or a decision into practice. ---
examples: The state will implement the new rules in June.
They implemented the program in three stages.
The law has been implemented very unevenly.
entries.русский: осуществлять, осуществить; внедрять, проводить в жизнь
entries.contrast: The verb is IM-pluh-ment; the noun (a tool) ends in a schwa: IM-pluh-muhnt.

entries.meaning: To try to persuade lawmakers to vote the way you want. ---
examples: Farm groups lobby hard every spring.
The industry lobbied against the new rule.
They have been lobbying Congress for years.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (lobby Congress), intransitive (lobby for a change)
entries.contrast: The -y follows a consonant: lobbies, lobbied, but lobbying. You lobby for what you want and against what you oppose.

entries.meaning: To officially free someone from a duty, a tax, or a rule. ---
examples: The bill would exempt small farms from the rule.
Churches exempted themselves from the fee for years.
Nobody has been exempted from the new requirement.
entries.contrast: The x sounds like gz: ig-ZEMPT. You exempt someone from something.

entries.meaning: To sell a state-owned service or industry to private owners. ---
examples: Some lawmakers want to privatize the postal service.
The country privatized its railways in the 1990s.
Water supplies have been privatized in several cities.

entries.meaning: To come into a country in order to live there permanently. ---
examples: Thousands immigrate legally every month.
Her grandparents immigrated in 1912.
He has immigrated to Canada with his family.
entries.contrast: You immigrate to the country you move into; you emigrate from the one you leave.

entries.meaning: To leave your own country in order to live in another. ---
examples: Many young engineers emigrate every year.
They emigrated from Ireland after the war.
Half the family has emigrated already.
entries.contrast: emigrate from the country you leave; immigrate to the one you enter.

entries.meaning: To set a maximum on how much of something is allowed. ---
examples: Several states limit campaign donations.
The chair limited debate to two hours.
Terms are limited to eight years in this state.
entries.contrast: The stress is on the first syllable, so the t does not double: limited, limiting.

entries.meaning: To be in favor of a person, a policy, or a plan. ---
examples: Most voters support the measure.
She supported the bill in committee and on the floor.
The proposal is supported by both parties.

entries.meaning: To have an effect on what someone decides or how something turns out.
examples: Big donors influence which bills get a hearing.
Foreign money influenced the last campaign.
The vote was influenced by one long speech.
entries.contrast: The verb takes a direct object: you influence someone, not "influence on" someone.
